title: The blind king asks
story: In Hastinapura the blind king Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what his sons and the Pandavas are doing on the field of Kurukshetra. Sanjaya, granted divine sight, begins to describe the battlefield.
set_pieces: dhritarashtra on his throne in a dark hall
sanjaya's eyes glowing as the battlefield appears
two armies under a rising sun

title: The conches sound
story: On a great chariot yoked with white horses, Krishna and Arjuna blow their divine conches, Panchajanya and Devadatta, and Bhima sounds Paundra. The sound shakes earth and sky.
set_pieces: white horses and golden chariot
conch raised to the lips against the sun
sound wave rippling dust across the armies

title: Between the two armies
story: Arjuna asks Krishna to place his chariot between the two armies so he can see whom he must fight. There he sees grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons and friends.
set_pieces: chariot rolling into the empty ground between armies
arjuna's eyes scanning faces
bhishma and drona across the field

title: The bow slips
story: Overcome by grief, Arjuna trembles, his mouth dries, the Gandiva bow slips from his hand, and he sinks down on the chariot seat, refusing to fight.
set_pieces: trembling hand
gandiva falling in slow motion
arjuna seated, head bowed, krishna watching

title: I am your disciple
story: Confused about his duty, Arjuna surrenders to Krishna as a disciple and asks to be taught what is truly good.
set_pieces: arjuna folding his hands
krishna turning towards him, light on his face

title: The soul never dies
story: Krishna teaches that the Self is never born and never dies; as a person casts off worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the embodied Self casts off worn-out bodies.
set_pieces: golden light inside a silhouette
cloth falling away and new cloth rising
eternal flame unmoved by wind

title: Act without clinging to results
story: Krishna tells Arjuna his right is to action alone, never to its fruits; he should not be driven by results nor attached to inaction.
set_pieces: arjuna's hand finding the bow again
arrow drawn back, eyes calm
fruit falling from a tree untouched

title: The one of steady wisdom
story: One whose wisdom is steady withdraws the senses from their objects as a tortoise draws in its limbs.
set_pieces: tortoise withdrawing into its shell at dawn
still lake reflecting the sky
arjuna's breathing slowing

title: No one can stop acting
story: Krishna explains that action is better than inaction, and that whatever a great person does, others follow.
set_pieces: sun rising and rivers flowing without pause
a leader stepping forward and an army following

title: Whenever dharma declines
story: Krishna reveals that whenever righteousness declines and unrighteousness rises, he manifests himself, age after age, to protect the good and restore dharma.
set_pieces: darkness spreading over a land
a pillar of light descending
ages turning like a great wheel

title: The fire of knowledge
story: As a blazing fire turns wood to ashes, the fire of knowledge burns all karma to ashes.
set_pieces: logs catching fire in slow motion
embers rising into a starry sky

title: Like a lotus leaf
story: One who acts, offering actions to the Divine and giving up attachment, is untouched by sin, as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
set_pieces: water droplets rolling off a lotus leaf
lotus opening at sunrise

title: Your mind: friend or enemy
story: Krishna teaches that one must lift oneself by oneself; the mind is the friend of one who has conquered it and the enemy of one who has not. A disciplined mind is like a lamp in a windless place that does not flicker.
set_pieces: a figure climbing out of mist
lamp flame perfectly still in a dark cave

title: The taste in water
story: Krishna says he is the taste in water, the light of the sun and the moon, the sacred syllable Om in the Vedas.
set_pieces: macro of water drop with light inside
sun and moon sharing one sky
om resonating as ripples

title: The last thought
story: Whoever remembers Krishna at the time of leaving the body attains his nature; whatever one remembers at the end, one goes to.
set_pieces: oil lamp burning down
a soul of light rising above a quiet river

title: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, water
story: Whoever offers Krishna with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, he accepts that offering of love.
set_pieces: small hands offering a single flower
leaf floating on a river towards the light

title: Among lights, the radiant sun
story: Krishna reveals his glories: he is the Self seated in the hearts of all beings, and among lights he is the radiant sun.
set_pieces: sun rising over the himalayas
light glowing in the heart of every warrior

title: The divine eye
story: Arjuna asks to see Krishna's universal form; Krishna grants him divine eyes, since he cannot see it with his own.
set_pieces: krishna touching arjuna's forehead
arjuna's eyes filling with starlight

title: Light of a thousand suns
story: If the light of a thousand suns blazed at once in the sky, it might resemble the splendour of that mighty Being.
set_pieces: sky splitting with a thousand suns
cosmic form with countless faces and arms, majestic and reverent
arjuna shielding his eyes

title: I am Time
story: Krishna declares that he is Time, the mighty destroyer of worlds, come to consume the people; even without Arjuna, the warriors arrayed will not survive.
set_pieces: galaxies turning in the cosmic form
armies seen as tiny against the vast form
arjuna kneeling in awe

title: Who is dear to me
story: Krishna describes the devotee dear to him: free of hatred, friendly and compassionate, free of ego, equal in pleasure and pain, forgiving, content and steady.
set_pieces: arjuna's face softening
an old man sharing bread with a stranger at dawn

title: The three gunas
story: Sattva, rajas and tamas, the three qualities born of nature, bind the imperishable Self to the body.
set_pieces: three streams of light, white, red and dark, weaving
a figure stepping free of the threads

title: The upside-down tree
story: Krishna describes the eternal ashvattha tree with roots above and branches below, whose leaves are the Vedic hymns; one who knows it knows the Vedas.
set_pieces: colossal tree hanging from the heavens
leaves glowing with script-like light

title: Take refuge in me
story: Krishna's final teaching: abandoning all other duties, take refuge in him alone; he will free Arjuna from all sins; do not grieve.
set_pieces: krishna extending his hand
arjuna's tears catching the light

title: My delusion is gone
story: Arjuna declares that his delusion is destroyed and his memory regained by Krishna's grace; he stands firm, free of doubt, and will act on Krishna's word. He lifts the Gandiva.
set_pieces: arjuna rising
gandiva lifted against the sun
armies turning to watch

title: Where Krishna and Arjuna are
story: Sanjaya concludes: wherever there is Krishna, the lord of yoga, and Arjuna, the archer, there will surely be fortune, victory, prosperity and righteousness.
set_pieces: sanjaya's vision fading
chariot silhouetted against the sun
banner of hanuman fluttering
